title: Replies translate IT terms literally instead of using them
what: The "Plain words" and native-language lines say to define every term and to name things by what they do; models read that as "translate every technical word" and write calques. Say instead: standard IT terms stay in their English form (merge, branch, commit, fast-forward, hook, CI, review, eval, worktree, flaky, lint), the prose around them is in the owner's language; relay's internal names (branches, files, slugs) still stay out; a relay-specific term gets its English name and a one-line definition the first time.
why: Owner, verbatim, 24 Oct: "Стиль твоего повествования кажется черезчур славянским, ты слишком отдаляешься от используемых технологических терминов, и некоторые из них ты переводишь прямо, при этом техническое значение они имеют только при употреблении в английском языке - и то среди IT специалистов". The front had written "перемотка" for fast-forward, "поезд" for merge train, "страховка слияния" for the merge hook, "платный прогон" for the paid eval run.
failing_case: 24 Oct front replies: "основная ветка просто перематывается", "страховка слияния откажет", "бесплатная проверка" for the gate.
pass_cases: The rule text says to keep standard IT terms in English and still keeps relay's internal names out; a paid check (several languages) shows a reply about a merge using "merge", "branch", "hook" in a Russian reply, and still defining a relay-only term once.
where: the rule that holds 'Working with me' (rules/*.md: Plain words, native language), roles that write to the owner
